messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: increased p95 token latency for hosted-generation in ap-southeast-1. p95 jumped from ~200ms -> ~1.6s over 6m. Error rate unchanged but queueing rising. Trigger: p95-over-1s-6m.

tay-oncall: oncall here, grabbing traces. anyone see heavy long-seq traffic or new rollouts in APAC? @lex-eng?

lex-eng: we rolled tokenizer-cache v2.0 to hosted-apac at 01:08 UTC to speed up subword lookups. quick canary was fine but not long-soak tested. change increases shared mmap regions; could be thrashing under memory pressure.

sre-max: infra view: a subset of pods with label tokenizer=v2 show CPU steal and elevated syscall latencies; KV cache hit is steady, but local tokenizer mmap faults spiking. looks like pager pressure on hosts with mixed tenancy (hosted + dedicated co-located).

tay-oncall: mitigation idea: 1) disable tokenizer-cache v2.0 for hosted pool (fast rollback), 2) temporarily move dedicated tenants off co-located hosts to reduce contention, 3) throttle non-SLA long-sequence requests. I'll flip 1 and 3 now.

tay-oncall: rollback tokenizer-cache on hosted-apac:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/feature/tokenizer_cache -d '{"region":"ap-southeast-1","variant":"v1","apply_now":true}'
```

deploy-bot: Feature toggle applied: tokenizer_cache -> v1 in ap-southeast-1 (requested by tay-oncall).

incident-bot: tokenizer mmap_faults on affected pods dropping ~75% within 40s after toggle. p95 improving from 1.6s -> ~760ms.

lex-eng: good. I'll prepare a follow-up patch to allocator to reduce mmap resident set and avoid thrash. For now, moving dedicated tenants:
```bash
# migrate dedicated tenant pool off shared nodes
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/compute/migrate -d '{"from":"shared-hosted-apac","to":"dedicated-pool-apac","tenants":["dedicated-*"]}'
```

deploy-bot: Migration job scheduled (requested by lex-eng). Nodes will rebalance over next ~5m.

ops-comm: drafting status page message. please review:

ops-comm: "Incident: Increased generation latency in APAC region. Impact: Some customers may experience slower response times for generation requests. Engineers have applied mitigations; no data loss reported. Next update in 30 minutes."

tay-oncall: add a brief mitigation list for customers: disabled tokenizer-cache v2, throttled non-SLA long-sequence requests, moving some tenants to dedicated pools. keep it short.

ops-comm: updated draft and posting.

status-bot: Status page created: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2145678912 (notif ids queued: notif-1417, notif-1418).

support-bot: Targeted customer emails queued for affected accounts (notif-1417/1418). Template used: short, actionable, and offers to open a support ticket for SLA customers.

incident-bot: Paging: SRE lead threshold reached. paging sre-max.

sre-max: on pager. I'll cordon any host showing >20% syscall wait and spin up replacement nodes in the apac pool. Also will temporarily lower process niceness for tokenizer workers to reduce preemption.

sre-max: cordon command:
```bash
kubectl -n serving cordon node/host-apac-11
kubectl -n serving drain node/host-apac-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

deploy-bot: Drain initiated for host-apac-11 (requested by sre-max).

incident-bot: telemetry: p95 steadying ~480-790ms after actions; mmap faults and syscall wait down on replaced hosts. Queue length decreasing but some queued long-seq requests >8s still draining.

lex-eng: quick experiment: toggle tokenizer warm cache for heavy-request paths to reduce cold mmap page faults. low-risk toggle.

lex-eng: enabling warm-cache for long-ctx:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/serving/ap-southeast-1/tokenizer-warm -d '{"enabled":true,"ttl_s":180}'
```

deploy-bot: Tokenizer warm-cache enabled for ap-southeast-1 (requested by lex-eng).

incident-bot: warm-cache increased local hit ratio on long-ctx hosts and p95 improved into 320-420ms range.

ops-comm: posting updated customer message: "Mitigations applied; performance improving. We'll monitor and post a resolution update when stable." (notif ids attached).

support-bot: support queue: 3 enterprise customers opened high-priority tickets (SUP-8820, SUP-8821, SUP-8822). ops-comm please coordinate direct updates.

zoe-pm: drafting internal exec note. bullets to confirm:
- Impact: elevated gen latency in APAC affecting some customers; no errors or data loss.
- Suspected: tokenizer-cache v2.0 mmap behavior causing page-fault storms under mixed tenancy.
- Mitigations: rolled tokenizer-cache to v1 for hosted, enabled tokenizer warm-cache, migrated dedicated tenants, cordoned noisy hosts, increased replacement nodes.
- Next: monitor 30m; if p95 >1s again -> consider full rollback of v2.0 across regions and schedule postmortem.

tay-oncall: monitoring for 30m. current p95 ~360ms. I'll hand off to sre-max at 02:45 UTC with this summary. If p95 >900ms or queued requests >50 for >5m, page oncall and escalate to eng lead.

sre-max: taking handoff. I'll watch for 2h and coordinate a remediation patch to tokenizer allocator with lex-eng. Also will collect host-level perf traces.

lex-eng: will open PR for allocator changes and run a soak test in staging with mixed dedicated/hosted tenancy to validate.

ops-comm: final customer note posted: "Performance improving; we will follow up with a detailed incident report once investigation completes." (support ticket IDs linked).

ops-comm: post-incident checklist posted in thread: collect mmap/pmem traces for 1h before/after rollout, tenant placement map, tokenizer v2 vs v1 perf matrix, soak test results, rollout gating update to require mixed-tenancy soak for allocator changes.

incident-bot: Thread state updated: investigating -> monitoring. last_update=2145680300
